resources.string: Use an existing router or portable Wi-Fi. Keep the iPhone and car on the same network with Internet access.
Existing Wi-Fi · Keep both devices on the same Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on. No car hotspot is needed.

Connect the car and iPhone to the same external Wi-Fi in system settings. Enter its exact name and WPA2 password below; leave the password empty only for an open network. Use WPA2 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode and disable client isolation on the router. DiPlay keeps this Wi-Fi connection and creates no hotspot.
Auto chooses a channel for you. Manual channels depend on what your car supports. Changes apply to the next Wi-Fi Direct connection.
Auto · 5 GHz and Auto · 2.4 GHz keep Wi-Fi Direct in that band and let the car choose the channel. If the car cannot use that band, the connection stops with a message instead of switching band.
Built-in car hotspot · Keep the car hotspot, Bluetooth and your iPhone’s Wi-Fi on.
Open Connection setup to save your built-in car hotspot details.
Wi-Fi Direct · Keep the car’s Wi-Fi switch, Bluetooth and your iPhone’s Wi-Fi on.

Use the car’s hotspot for the smoothest wireless CarPlay. You do not need to join it manually on your iPhone; DiPlay sends the hotspot details over Bluetooth. Select 5 GHz in car settings if available.
For cars without a hotspot. Requires the car’s Wi-Fi switch on. While the car searches for Wi-Fi networks, sound and picture may stutter every few seconds.
Hotspot is off · Turn it on in car settings.
Details saved · Check that the car hotspot is on before connecting.

An independent CarPlay receiver for Android head units. Wired and wireless connections run on the head unit, with local authentication. A standard iPhone can connect without a jailbreak, Mac, dongle or sign-in.\n\nThis preview uses an experimental accessory identity. Compatibility with every iPhone and head unit is still being tested. It is not an Apple-certified product.

Pair your iPhone with the car’s Bluetooth, keep Wi-Fi on, and allow CarPlay on the iPhone. Close any other phone-projection app.\n\nIf a previous projection app left its connection running, reset CarPlay Wi-Fi below and connect again. Your car’s normal internet Wi-Fi stays on.

3. Tap Check and enable below. This enables the cluster map and automatic theme following. An active CarPlay session reconnects once. You can then disconnect the computer.

Pick a finger count your head unit does not already use. BYD takes three-finger swipe-down for its air-conditioning panel.
Automatically turn on the car hotspot

Starts the saved car hotspot when DiPlay opens. Turning this on automatically requests the required permissions through ADB; allow the prompt on the car screen. Enable “Open after the car starts” for boot startup. Keeps the hotspot name and password and never turns it off.
Automatically turning on the car hotspot needs permission to modify system settings. Allow it below; otherwise it is requested when connecting.

Touch and hold the report text to select and copy it. You can use this if no sharing app is available.
Zoom the dashboard map with the wheel

BYD\'s custom key switches the volume keys between volume and dashboard map zoom while the dashboard shows the CarPlay map. A call always keeps the volume. On some cars the console volume sends the same keys, so it zooms too while zoom is on. Uses DiPlay\'s wheel key service; the note on the dashboard needs ADB.
Turn on the wheel key service · ADB
This head unit has no accessibility settings screen. Use the ADB button.
Press the wheel key for %1$s now…
Volume keys now zoom the dashboard map
Volume keys control the volume again

BYD\'s media key turns a joystick for CarPlay\'s centre screen on and off, like a car\'s rotary knob. While it is on, the volume roller or previous/next move the selection, play/pause selects and the custom key goes back; these keys then leave the music and volume alone. A call keeps the keys for the call. On some cars the console volume moves the selection too.
Keys from a paired Bluetooth keyboard, remote or rotary controller move and select in CarPlay, like a car’s rotary knob. The touchscreen keeps working. Applies at once.

How much charging current DiPlay offers the iPhone over USB. If wired CarPlay drops every few seconds and the iPhone reconnects by itself, the car\'s USB port may not supply enough power: try Reduced, then Low. The iPhone then charges more slowly. Applies at the next USB connection.
After 15 seconds without a press, and when a route starts, the keys go back to music and volume.
Volume roller or ⏮ ⏭ move · ⏯ selects · custom key goes back · media key ends
That key is already the %1$s key. Choose another key.

Opens Siri with a wheel key you choose while CarPlay is on the screen. A key that the car keeps for itself works only with the wheel key service, which also works when CarPlay is in the background. Without CarPlay, or during a call, the key keeps the car\'s own action.
Optional wheel key filtering for navigation volume during spoken guidance, dashboard map zoom, CarPlay joystick and call controls. No screen content is read.

Incoming and ongoing CarPlay calls show the caller on the instrument cluster, with the call time on the cluster and the head-up display, like BYD’s own CarPlay app. The car also turns the fan down during the call. Applies at once. Needs ADB over network on the head unit.
Drag the four green boundaries. Saving applies to the next CarPlay connection. A custom box replaces marker offsets; reset restores them.
Drag the green edges here and watch the outline on the cluster. Save applies the layout after reconnecting; Cancel keeps your current box.
The iPhone did not connect to CarPlay in time
Automatic retries stopped. Check the connection and retry manually.
Where CarPlay shows its apps, clock and status. Between Driver\'s side and Bottom it moves at once; Automatic leaves it to the iPhone and applies after a reconnect.
CarPlay in the head unit\'s split screen

When the head unit shows DiPlay in split screen, CarPlay redraws for that window instead of shrinking with black bars, and back to full screen without reconnecting. The window\'s size is learned the first time, so the picture fits exactly from the next connection. With the dock on Automatic, CarPlay then puts it at the bottom. Applies at the next connection.
Turn CarPlay with the screen without reconnecting

For head units whose screen turns. CarPlay gets a square picture holding a landscape and a portrait screen, so turning the screen redraws CarPlay instead of reconnecting. A larger square can increase video work and reduce smoothness, especially with Sharper on a large screen. If you rarely turn the screen, leaving this off may help. The custom safe area does not apply to a square picture. Applies at the next connection.
Setup did not verify every requested permission. Check each status below; enable network ADB and retry, or use the manual setup. Existing permissions are kept.

Opt in to unverified DiLink 3 call, voice and play/pause keys. Vehicle testing is still required. While a CarPlay call rings, next track answers and previous track declines. Disabled by default; dashboard call cards are a separate setting.
Shows DiPlay\’s panel beside CarPlay when this session declared one; unavailable sessions are greyed out.

CarPlay can move to two thirds of the screen while DiPlay shows a panel in the rest: on the passenger\'s side of a landscape screen, at the bottom of a portrait one (clock and, where it is read, the battery). Show and hide it from the in-session menu. Applies at the next connection.
Apps that support it, such as Apple Music, send up to about two minutes of music ahead, so short Wi-Fi gaps are not heard. Other apps keep the normal stream. Reconnects CarPlay.
Tries to reduce speaker echo sent to the other person during CarPlay calls. Results depend on the head unit. Applies at the next CarPlay connection.
Cuts bass from CarPlay call audio. This may change how voices sound. Applies at the next CarPlay connection.

Shows each main-screen CarPlay frame at the time the iPhone stamped on it plus a short delay, instead of as soon as it is decoded. The delay adjusts itself so that most frames are decoded in time; frames still not ready by their time are shown at once. Scrolling can look more even, but touches respond later. Picture adjustments do not apply. Reconnects CarPlay.

Detected %1$s for the selected video format. Uses a dedicated MTK low-latency decoder when available. Legacy OMX decoders instead try no-reorder plus low latency, then low latency alone. Automatically falls back if the decoder rejects or fails. It may reduce video delay, but some firmware can stutter or fail. Applies at the next CarPlay connection.

Sends the CarPlay picture straight to the head unit\'s compositor instead of drawing it inside the DiPlay window. Can lower the delay by about one screen refresh. Picture adjustments do not apply. Reconnects CarPlay.

Asks Qualcomm video decoders to output each frame as soon as it is decoded instead of holding the next ones, and shows each decoded frame from a dedicated thread without waiting for the next one to arrive. Can lower the delay by tens of milliseconds. Turn it off if the picture shows artifacts or freezes. Applies at the next connection.

Shows a counter in the top-right corner of CarPlay: frames shown per second (green from 50, yellow from 30, red below), frames received from the iPhone per second, and the decode time. A still screen shows few frames because the iPhone sends none.
CarPlay shows this icon and name in its app list. Tap it to return to the car\'s own screen. Changes apply the next time CarPlay connects.
Saved. CarPlay shows the new icon and name the next time it connects.
This head unit has no image picker.
Choose which settings the CarPlay swipe-down opens. The in-session menu stays available; its Open full DiPlay settings button always opens the home settings page.
When CarPlay is already running, tapping the DiPlay icon on the car\'s app list goes back to CarPlay. Turn this off to open the DiPlay home screen instead.
Pause car Bluetooth during CarPlay · needs ADB

The phone keeps its hands-free link to the car, so a call rings on both the car Bluetooth phone and CarPlay. While CarPlay runs, pause the car Bluetooth over ADB so calls ring on CarPlay only; with Bluetooth off, CarPlay calls play on the cabin speaker and microphone instead of the phone SCO. Bluetooth turns back on when CarPlay ends and before the next wireless handshake. Pairing is never touched. Changes apply on the next connection.

When the cluster switches to its small navi window, only part of the panel is visible. This keeps a second car-marker position for that window (default: right of centre) so the route shows inside it, and the custom turn card gets its own size and position inside the window; full-screen positions are unchanged. Changes reconnect the cluster map.
Default is three steps (30 %) right of centre. Adjust to wherever the small window sits on your cluster.
Usage Access granted · used if ADB cannot read the wheel navi mode.
Auto prefers ADB (same as pausing the dashboard map). If ADB is not approved, grant Usage Access so the cluster small-map state can still be followed, then reconnect.
Size of text and controls on DiPlay\'s own screens. Automatic enlarges them on large screens with a low density. CarPlay is not affected.
Back up or restore on a phone
Show a QR code so a phone browser on the same network can export or import DiPlay settings. The service stops when you leave the page.
Scan the code with the phone camera to open this page in its browser. Export saves a settings file, import loads one.
If the code does not open, try changing the IP address in your browser to %1$s.
No usable Wi-Fi network. Turn on the car hotspot or connect the phone to the car Wi-Fi first.
No camera? Open %1$s in a browser and enter the code %2$s.
Too many wrong codes were entered, so the code no longer works. Leave this page and open it again for a new one. The QR code still works.
This file is not a DiPlay settings backup.
Check for updates in the background
Once a day, DiPlay checks your selected update channel for a new version and shows it on the home screen. It never downloads without your tap.
CarPlay audio over the car\'s Bluetooth (experimental)

DiPlay offers the iPhone no CarPlay audio, so music, navigation and calls should go over the iPhone\'s Bluetooth connection with the car. Keep the iPhone paired with the car and choose Bluetooth as the car\'s audio source. If the sound plays on the iPhone instead, turn this off. Reconnects CarPlay.
Find your DiLink version, choose a connection and turn on the features that suit your car.
Found %1$s in the system version. Change it if that’s wrong.
DiPlay couldn’t read the DiLink version. Choose it below, or keep Not sure.
Choose how the iPhone reaches the car. Most cars work best with the car’s own hotspot on 5 GHz. Wi-Fi Direct needs no hotspot but may fall back to 2.4 GHz.
Suggested for %1$s. Turn on what you want now; everything stays in Settings and can be changed later.
The DiLink 4 cluster route is on. On DiLink 3 it stops the CarPlay map on the dashboard.
Connect your iPhone now. You can open this guide again from Settings.
Resolution, frame rate, connection and the other settings you just changed are not saved yet. Save and reconnect applies them.
Quick menu · swipe disabled (tap to change)

Stops DiPlay from requesting media audio focus while CarPlay music is active. Enable this if your head unit routes its physical volume buttons to DiPlay and they no longer adjust volume. Steering-wheel play, pause and track controls may stop working on head units that require focus. Applies at the next CarPlay connection.

Off (default): uses real vehicle data. On: away from the original car head unit, generates a 60-second simulated driving cycle (idle / accelerate / cruise / brake) and feeds it to the gauge card; takes effect immediately. Must stay off on the real car \u2014 the phone\u0027s map would show simulated range and battery.
Shows vehicle speed read from the car\'s own vehicle data. Hidden when a reading is unavailable. Changes apply immediately.
Let CarPlay occupy the OEM side-panel area on supported Harman head units. Applies when the CarPlay window next opens; other firmware may display incorrectly.

Names with Chinese or other non-English characters can leave CarPlay on “Getting CarPlay ready…”: some head units broadcast them in a form the iPhone doesn’t find. If that happens, rename the car hotspot with English letters and digits.

Over USB the iPhone can send navigation prompts and Siri’s spoken replies as 8 kHz phone-quality audio. This stops offering 8 and 16 kHz for that audio so the iPhone picks a higher rate. If prompts go silent, turn it off. Reconnects CarPlay.

This head unit’s Android Bluetooth reports a connection, but nothing reaches the iPhone: even a connection to a service that does not exist succeeds. Bluetooth here is handled by the maker’s own module, which apps cannot use, so wireless CarPlay cannot work on this head unit. Try a USB connection.
An old Wi-Fi Direct group may block this connection. Select Reset CarPlay Wi-Fi below, then connect again.
This head unit cannot send Bluetooth data to the iPhone. Wireless CarPlay cannot work here. Use a USB data cable.
Check that the car hotspot is on and its name and password match DiPlay settings. If available, use 5 GHz, then retry.
Keep Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on. On the iPhone, join the car hotspot and enable Auto-Join, then retry. Save a diagnostic report if it still fails.
Allow the requested USB, Nearby devices or Location permissions for DiPlay on the head unit, then retry.
Use a USB data port and a data-capable cable. Unlock the iPhone, approve Trust and CarPlay, then retry.
Unlock the iPhone, enable Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and pair it with the head unit. Keep it nearby, then retry.
Retry the connection. If it fails again, return to DiPlay and save a report under Settings → Diagnostics.
Keep the head unit\'s Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on and the iPhone unlocked nearby, then retry. If it keeps failing, forget the car on the iPhone under Settings → General → CarPlay and connect again.
Make sure the head unit and the iPhone are on the same Wi-Fi network and its name and password match DiPlay settings, then retry.
Get the report on a phone
Scan the code with the phone camera to open this page in its browser, then choose Download report. Keep this screen open until the download has finished.
Show the song title, artist and album as a card on the instrument cluster. The card has its own position and size sliders.
Draw the album cover on the media card. Turn off for a text-only card, which is easier to read on the small cluster panel.
Song title, artist and album each get one line. A line that is still too long scrolls sideways instead of being cut off.
Disconnect the car’s Bluetooth during CarPlay

The /info disableBluetooth key only stops Bluetooth audio negotiation — the iPhone still opens A2DP/HFP. This cuts the car side: OFF does nothing, Audio drops A2DP_SINK (music stops coming from the car), Full also drops HFP (calls and ringtones stop too), All drops every link.
Navigation prompts lower the media volume

Off (default): navigation prompts play over the music at full volume. On: the music is lowered while navigation is speaking, then restored a few seconds after the last prompt. The music volume itself is never changed, only how loud it plays alongside navigation.
How loud the music stays while navigation is talking. Lower means the prompt stands out more; higher keeps the music closer to normal.

Off (default): navigation prompts overlay other audio without interrupting it — this is what lets the car’s own map and an aftermarket map app speak at the same time. On: navigation takes audio focus, so the head unit can duck or pause other audio while it talks. Turn it on if navigation prompts are too quiet or get drowned out.

Off (default): nothing changes. On: marks our audio request as “must stay audible” so the head unit cannot silence or duck it. The car’s own apps set this flag; enabling it may stop CarPlay audio being muted when other audio policies kick in. Turn it off if audio gets stuck at full volume.

Off (default): no output. On: when audio starts playing, log the head unit’s own volume groups and current levels (read-only, changes nothing). Useful for confirming how the car maps CarPlay audio to its navigation and music volume sliders. Read the log with: adb logcat -s NavVolumeFollower
Reduce CarPlay navigation guidance without changing music or call volume. Applies immediately; your head unit’s navigation volume still works.
Show the caller and call duration on the instrument cluster during a CarPlay call.
During a CarPlay call, the steering wheel answer key answers and the hang-up key ends or declines it. Outside a call the keys keep working for the car\'s own phone.
What the instrument cluster shows and where the cards sit
While a CarPlay call is ringing, the answer key answers it and the hang-up key declines it. Outside a call the keys keep working for the car and for music.
Press the key you want to use
Asks SuperUni for the physical instrument channel so the CarPlay map reaches the dashboard. Without it the cluster falls back to the direct presentation path.
SuperUni is not installed on this car; the direct presentation path is used instead.

Draws the rev counter, power, range or fuel, battery, mileage and tyre pressure on the instrument cluster. The card reads the car\u0027s own sensors, so it works on any car and needs no phone support. Choose which readings to show and adjust the text size. Only the readings the car actually provides are shown \u2014 a missing value is left out rather than faked. Changes apply immediately.
Hidden readings stay hidden on the cluster too \u2014 nothing is faked. A car that does not provide a value simply skips it.
